title: Sync to upstream v2.0.1 — activate Permit2 on Polygon
body:
## What

Sync this fork to **upstream x402-rs v2.0.1** (134 upstream commits) while preserving the Polygon-specific commits, plus one follow-up fix required by an upstream API change.

- Merge `upstream/main` (v1.3.0-era → **v2.0.1**) into the fork.
- Preserve Polygon commits: env-driven facilitator config (`config_from_env`), structured JSON logging, and the `0xpolygon/x402-facilitator` CI image.
- Fix: `RpcConfig.http` became `LiteralOrEnv<Url>` upstream — adapt `config_from_env()` (`facilitator/src/config.rs`).

## Why

Production (`main`) cannot settle Permit2 payments on Polygon: it hard-codes Permit2 proxy addresses that were **never deployed on-chain**, and lacks the EIP-2612 `settleWithPermit` (gasless-approval) path. v2.0.1 brings:
- the **correct, on-chain-deployed** proxy addresses (`0x402085c248…0001` exact, `0x4020A4f3b7…0002` upto — both verified live on Polygon mainnet **and** Amoy), and
- the EIP-2612 `settleWithPermit` path.

This is required for the wallet team's **x402 smart-session signer**, which relies on Permit2.

## Verification

Run against this branch with `--features full`:

- **Unit tests:** 129 passed, 0 failed (workspace excluding the pre-existing TRON failure — see below).
- **Release binary:** `cargo build -p x402-facilitator --features full --release --locked` ✅
- **Docker image:** builds (`x402-facilitator:v2.0.1`).
- **Container boot (env-driven, mainnet 137):** `/health` → 200; `/supported` lists `exact` + `upto` on `eip155:137`; logs confirm the env-config fallback and structured JSON logging.
- **Live end-to-end Permit2 settles on Polygon mainnet (the definitive proof):** client signed a Permit2 authorization → facilitator verified → settled on-chain via the deployed exact Permit2 proxy `0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001` (status success in both cases). Two independent tokens:
  - **USDC** (supports EIP-3009): tx `0x0d7b57ab899e9d10a697f45a5345b84a7a439a08963c01cc7d7fcd2a0ffa2937`; moved 0.01 USDC, allowance consumed by exactly the payment.
  - **USDT0** (does **not** support EIP-3009 — so Permit2 is the only rail): tx `0xbb81a39a96d2c381eb5b5bca7c61c402d8cf394a28b3a79056d731ac2b5325ad`; moved 0.01 USDT, allowance consumed by exactly the payment. This conclusively exercises the Permit2 path for an arbitrary ERC-20.

## Known issue

- One pre-existing **upstream** unit-test failure: `x402-chain-tron::networks::tests::permit2_proxies`. It fails identically on pristine `upstream/main` (not introduced by this sync), and TRON is unused by this deployment.

## Caveats

- The sync also pulls upstream TRON / Aptos / Solana changes (full v2.0.1). A partial cherry-pick was rejected because it would re-introduce the proxy-address / Permit2-witness mismatch.
- Bundled-approval for undeployed wallets is **EIP-2612-specific** (`settleWithPermit`) — works for USDC and other 2612 tokens.

title: chore: stop advertising unsupported `upto` scheme on Polygon facilitator
body:
## What

Stop advertising the **`upto`** scheme (`v2-eip155-upto`) on the Polygon facilitator. It is removed from `config_from_env()` so it no longer appears in `/supported` (and `/health`), and `verify`/`settle` for an upto payload return a graceful `unsupported_scheme`. **The upto implementation is left fully compiled in** — this only stops registering the scheme.

## Why

Live testing against the deployed Amoy facilitator showed `upto` is broken on the multi-instance deployment:

- The `upto` scheme binds each payment to **one specific facilitator signer** (the Permit2 witness `facilitator` field; the on-chain proxy enforces `msg.sender == witness.facilitator`).
- The deployment runs **≥3 instances behind a load balancer, each with a disjoint signer set**. `supported()` advertises a random signer from the responding instance, but verify/settle are round-robined to other instances → `500 "Missing signing credential for 0x…"` (~2/3 of attempts). In some cases funds moved on-chain while the client received a 402 (settle/response desync).
- `upto` is **Permit2-only by design** (EIP-3009 can't express "up to" amounts), so there is no fallback rail.

The proper fix (shared signer set across instances, or signer-aware routing) is an infrastructure effort. Until then, advertising `upto` misleads consumers into attempting a flow that mostly fails. `exact` (v1/v2, both EIP-3009 and Permit2 rails) is unaffected and verified working (16 live Amoy settles).

## Changes

- `facilitator/src/config.rs` — remove the `v2-eip155-upto` `SchemeConfig` from `config_from_env()` (with an explanatory comment); update the `config_from_env` unit test to assert upto is absent (schemes len 3→2).
- `facilitator/config.json.example` — drop the `v2-eip155-upto` entry so a copied config doesn't re-enable it.
- **Not changed:** the `V2Eip155Upto` blueprint wiring (`run.rs`), the builder impl (`schemes.rs`), and the entire `crates/chains/x402-chain-eip155/src/v2_eip155_upto/**` implementation — all retained, just unused, so re-enabling is a one-line change once infra supports it.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p x402-facilitator --features full config` — passes (2/2).
- Booted locally (env-driven, `CHAIN_ID=80002`): `/supported` and `/health` list only `exact` (v2 `eip155:80002` + v1 `polygon-amoy`), **no `upto`**.
- upto payload → `POST /verify` and `POST /settle` return `unsupported_scheme` (HTTP 400), no crash.
- The deployed facilitator uses the env-var config path (no config.json is copied in the Dockerfile), so this change covers production once the new image is deployed.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- Infra fix to actually support `upto` (shared signer set or signer-aware routing), then re-register the scheme.
- Optional: skip the `v2-eip155-upto-*` conformance tests (they spawn a single-instance facilitator where upto still works, so they're unaffected by this change).
